en.greeting: Hi! Today is about sounding careful and credible: softening a claim so it matches the evidence, and saying exactly how sure you are. It's the language of good reports, research and professional emails. Let's start with why it matters.

steps.title: Why hedge?
steps.text: First, a word you'll use all lesson: hedging.
steps.body:
**Hedging** = softening a **claim** (a statement that something is true) so it matches the evidence: not 100% sure, not true in every case. You know the start from B2: **might have**, **most** instead of *all*, **tend to**.

The habit to change: in many Indonesian offices people soften a lot when they speak (*mungkin, sepertinya*), but reports say *pasti* or *terbukti* with little data. In English reports, a 100% claim without strong evidence sounds **unscientific**. But don't hedge facts: *The meeting is on Monday.*

steps.title: Softening a claim
steps.text: Here are the softeners at work in real reports.
steps.body: **tend to** + base verb is a verb, not an adjective: *They tend to…*, never `They are tend to` (from *mereka cenderung*). In **It would appear that…**, *would* doesn't mean 'if': it just sounds softer and more formal. **arguably** marks an opinion you can defend with reasons.

examples.en: Startups in Jakarta tend to hire people through personal networks.
examples.id: Startup di Jakarta cenderung merekrut orang lewat jaringan pribadi.

examples.en: The new booking system seems to be faster.
examples.id: Sistem pemesanan yang baru tampaknya lebih cepat.

examples.en: It would appear that the shipment was sent to the wrong warehouse.
examples.id: Tampaknya kiriman itu dikirim ke gudang yang salah.

examples.en: Arguably, public transport is the city's biggest challenge.
examples.id: Bisa dibilang, transportasi umum adalah tantangan terbesar kota ini.

examples.en: The campaign worked to some extent.
examples.id: Kampanye itu berhasil sampai batas tertentu.

examples.en: In some cases, patients had to wait more than three hours.
examples.id: Dalam beberapa kasus, pasien harus menunggu lebih dari tiga jam.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina is writing an HR report about staff turnover at her company in Bandung.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Anak muda cenderung lebih sering berganti pekerjaan.
question.solution: Young people tend to change jobs more often.
question.explanation: **tend** is a verb: **tend to** + base verb (**change**), with no *are* before it. It softens the claim: it's a general pattern, not true of every young person.

steps.title: Not too strong, not too weak
steps.text: Now the most important choice in a report: how strong is your verb?
steps.body:
**proves** (membuktikan): only for very strong, final evidence. One study almost never proves anything. **shows** (menunjukkan): clear evidence. **suggests / indicates** (mengindikasikan): a sign, but more research is needed. Here *suggest* isn't *menyarankan*.

A survey finds that two things happen together; it doesn't show one causes the other. So: `This proves that social media causes depression.` → **This suggests that social media may contribute to depression.**

But **one hedge is enough**: `It may possibly perhaps be true.` → **It may be true.**

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dr. Wulan asked 120 employees at one bank in Jakarta about their commute. Those with longer commutes reported more stress.

question.prompt: Which sentence fits Dr. Wulan's report best?
options: This proves that long commutes cause stress.
This suggests that long commutes may contribute to stress.
This may possibly suggest that long commutes could perhaps be linked to stress.
question.explanation: One survey at one bank gives a sign, not proof, and it shows a connection, not a cause: **suggests** + **may contribute to** matches the evidence. `proves … cause` is far too strong; the third sentence piles up four hedges.

steps.title: Too many hedges
steps.text: Sari's supervisor reads her conclusion: 'It might perhaps possibly be the case that flexible hours could improve staff wellbeing.' The evidence is mixed.

options: Flexible hours may improve staff wellbeing.
Flexible hours improve staff wellbeing.
It might possibly be the case that flexible hours could improve staff wellbeing.
question.explanation: With mixed evidence you need a hedge, but **one** is enough: **may improve**. Without any hedge the claim is too strong; the third version still has three hedges (*might, possibly, could*).

steps.title: The certainty scale
steps.text: Next: saying exactly how sure you are. Here's the scale, from the strongest to the weakest.
steps.body:
**almost certainly** and **probably** go after *will* / *be*, before the main verb: *Costs will probably rise.* **likely** is an adjective, so it needs *be*: **It is likely that…** / **Costs are likely to rise**, never `It likely that`.

It's a guide, not a ruler: *probably* = *it is likely that*. And keep *pasti* honest: in a report, **clearly** and **undoubtedly** are only for very strong evidence.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan is writing a risk report and wants to rank four phrases.

question.prompt: Which list goes from the MOST certain to the LEAST certain?
options: probably → almost certainly → it is unlikely that → possibly
possibly → probably → almost certainly → it is unlikely that
almost certainly → probably → possibly → it is unlikely that
question.explanation: **almost certainly** (hampir pasti) → **probably** (kemungkinan besar) → **possibly** (mungkin) → **it is unlikely that** (kemungkinan kecil). The other lists mix up the order.

steps.title: Certainty in real sentences
steps.text: Here's the scale in sentences from work and the news. Watch one tiny word: little.
steps.body: **There is little evidence** = almost none (negative). **There is a little evidence** = some (positive): the opposite message! **will likely** (*Costs will likely rise*) is common in American English; British English prefers **will probably** or **are likely to**.

examples.en: The new MRT line will almost certainly open later than planned.
examples.id: Jalur MRT baru itu hampir pasti dibuka lebih lambat dari rencana.

examples.en: It is highly likely that the board will approve the budget.
examples.id: Sangat mungkin dewan direksi akan menyetujui anggaran itu.

examples.en: Rice prices are likely to rise before Lebaran.
examples.id: Harga beras kemungkinan besar naik menjelang Lebaran.

examples.en: It is unlikely that the client will sign before Friday.
examples.id: Kemungkinan kecil klien itu akan tanda tangan sebelum hari Jumat.

examples.en: There is little evidence that the new logo increased sales.
examples.id: Hampir tidak ada bukti bahwa logo baru itu meningkatkan penjualan.

steps.title: Stronger or weaker?
steps.text: Budi's forecast says: 'It is likely that office rents in Surabaya will rise next year.' His manager thinks that's too confident and asks for a weaker version.

question.prompt: Which sentence is WEAKER (less certain) than Budi's?
options: Office rents in Surabaya will almost certainly rise next year.
Office rents in Surabaya could rise next year.
It is highly likely that office rents in Surabaya will rise next year.
question.explanation: **could** (mungkin) is lower on the scale than **it is likely that** (kemungkinan besar). **almost certainly** and **it is highly likely that** are both stronger, the opposite of what the manager asked for.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page, to keep next to you when you write a report.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Hedging and certainty
artifact.intro: Match the claim to the evidence: strong evidence, strong words; weak or one-study evidence, one hedge.
rows: after will / be: It will almost certainly…
a pattern with exceptions; not 'are tend to'
it looks true; appear is more formal
to some extent / in some cases
sampai batas tertentu / dalam beberapa kasus
one study; may contribute to, not causes
tips: One hedge per claim: 'may', not 'may possibly perhaps'.
Don't hedge facts: The meeting is on Monday.
Keep pasti and terbukti for what you can really prove: in English reports, use clearly or proves only with strong evidence.

examples.en: The survey suggests that long meetings may reduce productivity.
examples.id: Survei itu mengindikasikan bahwa rapat yang panjang bisa menurunkan produktivitas.

examples.en: Junior staff tend to stay late before a deadline.
examples.id: Staf junior cenderung pulang terlambat menjelang tenggat.

examples.en: Arguably, Bandung has the most creative startup scene in Indonesia.
examples.id: Bisa dibilang, Bandung punya ekosistem startup paling kreatif di Indonesia.

examples.en: The new toll road will almost certainly reduce travel time to the airport.
examples.id: Jalan tol baru itu hampir pasti mengurangi waktu tempuh ke bandara.

steps.text: Two videos and a reference page on hedging in academic writing, all in English, if you'd like more examples.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini tentang terdengar hati-hati dan bisa dipercaya: melunakkan klaim supaya sesuai dengan buktinya, dan menyatakan dengan tepat seberapa yakin kamu. Ini bahasa laporan, riset dan email profesional yang baik. Kita mulai dari kenapa ini penting.

steps.title: Kenapa perlu hedging?
steps.text: Pertama, satu kata yang akan kamu pakai sepanjang pelajaran: hedging.
steps.body:
**Hedging** = melunakkan **klaim** (pernyataan bahwa sesuatu itu benar) supaya sesuai dengan buktinya: tidak 100% yakin, tidak berlaku di semua kasus. Awalnya sudah kamu kenal di B2: **might have**, **most** sebagai ganti *all*, **tend to**.

Kebiasaan yang perlu diubah: di banyak kantor di Indonesia orang sangat melunakkan ucapan (*mungkin, sepertinya*), tapi laporan menulis *pasti* atau *terbukti* dengan data yang sedikit. Di laporan berbahasa Inggris, klaim 100% tanpa bukti kuat terdengar **tidak ilmiah**. Tapi jangan melunakkan fakta: *The meeting is on Monday.*

steps.title: Melunakkan klaim
steps.text: Ini contoh pelunak yang dipakai di laporan sungguhan.
steps.body: **tend to** + kata kerja dasar adalah kata kerja, bukan kata sifat: *They tend to…*, tidak pernah `They are tend to` (dari *mereka cenderung*). Dalam **It would appear that…**, *would* tidak berarti 'kalau': hanya terdengar lebih lunak dan formal. **arguably** menandai pendapat yang bisa kamu pertahankan dengan alasan.

examples.en: Startups in Jakarta tend to hire people through personal networks.
examples.id: Startup di Jakarta cenderung merekrut orang lewat jaringan pribadi.

examples.en: The new booking system seems to be faster.
examples.id: Sistem pemesanan yang baru tampaknya lebih cepat.

examples.en: It would appear that the shipment was sent to the wrong warehouse.
examples.id: Tampaknya kiriman itu dikirim ke gudang yang salah.

examples.en: Arguably, public transport is the city's biggest challenge.
examples.id: Bisa dibilang, transportasi umum adalah tantangan terbesar kota ini.

examples.en: The campaign worked to some extent.
examples.id: Kampanye itu berhasil sampai batas tertentu.

examples.en: In some cases, patients had to wait more than three hours.
examples.id: Dalam beberapa kasus, pasien harus menunggu lebih dari tiga jam.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina sedang menulis laporan HR tentang pergantian karyawan di kantornya di Bandung.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Anak muda cenderung lebih sering berganti pekerjaan.
question.solution: Young people tend to change jobs more often.
question.explanation: **tend** adalah kata kerja: **tend to** + kata kerja dasar (**change**), tanpa *are* di depannya. Klaimnya jadi lebih lunak: ini pola umum, bukan berlaku untuk setiap anak muda.

steps.title: Tidak terlalu kuat, tidak terlalu lemah
steps.text: Sekarang pilihan terpenting di laporan: seberapa kuat kata kerjamu?
steps.body:
**proves** (membuktikan): hanya untuk bukti yang sangat kuat dan final. Satu penelitian hampir tidak pernah membuktikan apa pun. **shows** (menunjukkan): bukti yang jelas. **suggests / indicates** (mengindikasikan): ada tanda, tapi perlu riset lagi. Di sini *suggest* bukan *menyarankan*.

Survei menemukan dua hal terjadi bersamaan; itu tidak menunjukkan yang satu menyebabkan yang lain. Jadi: `This proves that social media causes depression.` → **This suggests that social media may contribute to depression.**

Tapi **satu pelunak sudah cukup**: `It may possibly perhaps be true.` → **It may be true.**

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dr. Wulan bertanya kepada 120 karyawan di satu bank di Jakarta tentang perjalanan mereka ke kantor. Yang perjalanannya lebih lama melaporkan stres yang lebih tinggi.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang paling cocok untuk laporan Dr. Wulan?
options: This proves that long commutes cause stress.
This suggests that long commutes may contribute to stress.
This may possibly suggest that long commutes could perhaps be linked to stress.
question.explanation: Satu survei di satu bank memberi tanda, bukan bukti, dan menunjukkan hubungan, bukan sebab: **suggests** + **may contribute to** sesuai dengan buktinya. `proves … cause` terlalu kuat; kalimat ketiga menumpuk empat pelunak.

steps.title: Terlalu banyak pelunak
steps.text: Atasan Sari membaca kesimpulannya: 'It might perhaps possibly be the case that flexible hours could improve staff wellbeing.' Buktinya beragam (ada yang mendukung, ada yang tidak).

options: Flexible hours may improve staff wellbeing.
Flexible hours improve staff wellbeing.
It might possibly be the case that flexible hours could improve staff wellbeing.
question.explanation: Dengan bukti yang beragam kamu butuh pelunak, tapi **satu** saja cukup: **may improve**. Tanpa pelunak sama sekali klaimnya terlalu kuat; versi ketiga masih punya tiga pelunak (*might, possibly, could*).

steps.title: Skala kepastian
steps.text: Berikutnya: menyatakan dengan tepat seberapa yakin kamu. Ini skalanya, dari yang paling kuat ke yang paling lemah.
steps.body:
**almost certainly** dan **probably** diletakkan setelah *will* / *be*, sebelum kata kerja utama: *Costs will probably rise.* **likely** adalah kata sifat, jadi butuh *be*: **It is likely that…** / **Costs are likely to rise**, tidak pernah `It likely that`.

Ini panduan, bukan penggaris: *probably* = *it is likely that*. Dan jujurlah dengan *pasti*: di laporan, **clearly** dan **undoubtedly** hanya untuk bukti yang sangat kuat.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Hasan sedang menulis laporan risiko dan ingin mengurutkan empat frasa.

question.prompt: Daftar mana yang urut dari PALING yakin ke PALING TIDAK yakin?
options: probably → almost certainly → it is unlikely that → possibly
possibly → probably → almost certainly → it is unlikely that
almost certainly → probably → possibly → it is unlikely that
question.explanation: **almost certainly** (hampir pasti) → **probably** (kemungkinan besar) → **possibly** (mungkin) → **it is unlikely that** (kemungkinan kecil). Daftar lainnya urutannya tercampur.

steps.title: Kepastian dalam kalimat nyata
steps.text: Ini skalanya dalam kalimat dari dunia kerja dan berita. Perhatikan satu kata kecil: little.
steps.body: **There is little evidence** = hampir tidak ada bukti (negatif). **There is a little evidence** = ada sedikit bukti (positif): pesannya berlawanan! **will likely** (*Costs will likely rise*) umum dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika; bahasa Inggris British lebih memilih **will probably** atau **are likely to**.

examples.en: The new MRT line will almost certainly open later than planned.
examples.id: Jalur MRT baru itu hampir pasti dibuka lebih lambat dari rencana.

examples.en: It is highly likely that the board will approve the budget.
examples.id: Sangat mungkin dewan direksi akan menyetujui anggaran itu.

examples.en: Rice prices are likely to rise before Lebaran.
examples.id: Harga beras kemungkinan besar naik menjelang Lebaran.

examples.en: It is unlikely that the client will sign before Friday.
examples.id: Kemungkinan kecil klien itu akan tanda tangan sebelum hari Jumat.

examples.en: There is little evidence that the new logo increased sales.
examples.id: Hampir tidak ada bukti bahwa logo baru itu meningkatkan penjualan.

steps.title: Lebih kuat atau lebih lemah?
steps.text: Prakiraan Budi berbunyi: 'It is likely that office rents in Surabaya will rise next year.' Manajernya merasa itu terlalu yakin dan meminta versi yang lebih lemah.

question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang LEBIH LEMAH (kurang yakin) daripada kalimat Budi?
options: Office rents in Surabaya will almost certainly rise next year.
Office rents in Surabaya could rise next year.
It is highly likely that office rents in Surabaya will rise next year.
question.explanation: **could** (mungkin) lebih rendah di skala daripada **it is likely that** (kemungkinan besar). **almost certainly** dan **it is highly likely that** sama-sama lebih kuat, kebalikan dari permintaan manajernya.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman, untuk disimpan di dekatmu saat menulis laporan.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Hedging dan kepastian
artifact.intro: Sesuaikan klaim dengan buktinya: bukti kuat, kata yang kuat; bukti lemah atau satu penelitian, satu pelunak.
rows: hanya untuk bukti yang sangat kuat
setelah will / be: It will almost certainly…
pola umum dengan pengecualian; bukan 'are tend to'
to some extent / in some cases
sampai batas tertentu / dalam beberapa kasus
satu penelitian; may contribute to, bukan causes
tips: Satu pelunak per klaim: 'may', bukan 'may possibly perhaps'.
Jangan melunakkan fakta: The meeting is on Monday.
Simpan pasti dan terbukti untuk hal yang benar-benar bisa dibuktikan: di laporan berbahasa Inggris, pakai clearly atau proves hanya dengan bukti kuat.

examples.en: The survey suggests that long meetings may reduce productivity.
examples.id: Survei itu mengindikasikan bahwa rapat yang panjang bisa menurunkan produktivitas.

examples.en: Junior staff tend to stay late before a deadline.
examples.id: Staf junior cenderung pulang terlambat menjelang tenggat.

examples.en: Arguably, Bandung has the most creative startup scene in Indonesia.
examples.id: Bisa dibilang, Bandung punya ekosistem startup paling kreatif di Indonesia.

examples.en: The new toll road will almost certainly reduce travel time to the airport.
examples.id: Jalan tol baru itu hampir pasti mengurangi waktu tempuh ke bandara.

steps.text: Dua video dan satu halaman rujukan tentang hedging dalam tulisan akademik, semuanya dalam bahasa Inggris, kalau kamu mau contoh lebih banyak.
